source.author: ov
source.text: Dextra laevaque deorum atria nobilium valvis celebrantur apertis plebs habitat diversa locis: hac parte potentes caelicolae clarique suos posuere penates.
source.text_original: Dextra laevaque deorum / atria nobilium valvis celebrantur apertis / (plebs habitat diversa locis): hac parte potentes / caelicolae clarique suos posuere penates.
source.text_english: On the right and on the left the noble halls of the gods are frequented, with their doors thrown open; the common folk live in separate quarters: in this part the powerful dwellers in heaven, the famous ones, have set up their household gods.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: si domos habent, consequens est ut et urbes habeant, et quidem auctore Nasone, qui ait: plebs habitat diuersa locis, a fronte potentes caelicolae clarique suos posuere penates.
reuse.text_original: si domos habent, consequens est ut et urbes habeant, et quidem auctore Nasone, qui ait: plebs habitat diuersa locis, a fronte potentes caelicolae clarique suos posuere penates.
reuse.text_english: If they have houses, it follows that they also have cities, and indeed on the authority of Naso, who says: the common people dwell in scattered places; in the forefront the powerful gods and the famous dwellers in heaven have set up their own household gods.
